fullText:
Great paper from NVIDIA sharing an open midtraining recipe for agentic coding.

NVIDIA kept SFT identical and added one midtraining stage. SWE-bench Multilingual went from 55.8 to 62.8 on Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.

The stage sits between pretraining and post-training. It trains at 256K context on 500B tokens of natural software-engineering data, such as packed repositories, pull requests, commit histories and build logs, plus a small share of agent traces.

On the same model, SWE-bench Verified rose from 60.7 to 64.5 and SWE-bench Pro from 32.0 to 35.5. On the larger Nemotron 3.5 Super, DeepSWE rose from 11.7 to 15.7.

They also explain how they evaluated the recipe. Base-model proxy metrics did not predict post-training results, so every data choice was scored with short fixed SFT runs.

If you train coding agents, the recipe and its ablations are published.

https://t.co/SJ7JHdd1HY

fullText:
腾讯昨天开源的Hy-Memory 2.0，让不同AI Agent共享记忆，不用每换一个AI工具就从头开始了

比如你在Cursor里讨论过的项目，之后切换到Codex、WorkBuddy、Hermes等，不必每次再从头解读一遍，如果相关记忆已被保存并成功召回，新Agent就能在已有上下文上继续工作

这是Hy-Memory 2.0配套应用“MemHub”的能力，把分散在不同AI工具里的历史对话和工作经验汇入统一的记忆体系，让不同Agent复用相关上下文

另外，Memory 2.0还针对不同场景设计了三类记忆机制，让AI能记住对话，记住任务进展、经验的适用条件，以及代码为什么这么改

Chat Memory：记住人和对话
提取跨会话事实、组织长期记忆，并处理重复信息和事实冲突，减少每次对话都要重新了解用户的问题

Working Memory：记住任务与经验
将任务事实和可复用经验分开管理，事实层记录做了什么、结果如何；经验层提炼哪些方法有效、适用于什么条件。重点是让Agent有机会把过去的解决方案复用到下一次任务中

Coding Memory：记住代码如何演进
将代码Diff、修改上下文和版本演进链纳入记忆体系，让编程Agent不只看到当前代码，还能追溯历史修改及其背景，为持续开发提供上下文

配套还提供了专门针对长期记忆写入训练的模型：Hy-Memory-30B-A3B，专门学习如何筛选、组织和更新值得长期保存的信息

这套方案等于说把Agent记忆从简单的事实提取和检索，扩展到了任务经验沉淀、代码演进追踪以及跨工具的上下文复用上

#HyMemory  #AIMemory #AI记忆

有人开源了小学全学科知识图谱：os-taxonomy，数据涵盖1590个知识点、3221条依赖关系

可以拿来做AI家教或者RAG外挂，也有人把它包成MCP，让Agent直接查询“学这个之前要掌握什么”、“到这个目标的最近路径”

我认为值得关注的地方是：它把知识之间的先后依赖关系显式化了，AI不只能回答孩子眼前的问题，还可以结合测评结果识别可能缺失的前置知识，来规划下一步应该学什么

比如说，孩子要理解水为什么会沸腾，就需要先理解温度、热量以及水的状态变化

那知识图谱能把这些前置知识与后续概念连接起来，让学习不再只是孤立的硬记课本内容

它解决了教育的三个关键问题：
学什么？ 把分散的课程内容拆成结构化知识单元
先学什么？ 显式标记知识之间的依赖关系

怎么学？ 为AI辅导、知识缺口诊断、个性化学习路径提供结构化基础

他们自家也基于这个图谱，做了一个孩子可以交互实验式学习的产品

图谱目前覆盖了科学、数学、英语等8个学科，对齐的是美英课标，NGSS/Common Core/英国国家课程

Last year I thought Threads was an existential risk to X. 

When Meta puts its full weight behind something -- by injecting the app into Instagram, it’s DEFCON 5:

You have to squeeze out every last drop of growth from all available surfaces to save the app.

However, I started to realize that the opposite was happening:

It was strengthening X.

If you look at any announcement by Zuck, you will see the most rude & toxic comments on the internet. 

But when he makes those same announcements on X, people are thrilled about how he’s pushing humanity forward. X is a place where people are excited about the future, so it’s no surprise he and his top lieutenants are using it more than their own app.

Threads — and Bluesky — have effectively quarantined some of the worst people on the internet. 

And so I had an epiphany: those apps are X’s anti-abuse systems.

fullText:
after an exciting week of launches (muse wonder [full] & muse spark open), i want to write a note of appreciation to the amazing research teams at meta superintelligence labs on reaching such a special milestone ♥️

we started MSL and TBD a little more than a year ago and set a goal of producing a frontier model within a year or so. given where llama4 landed, that was an incredibly audacious goal, and we knew it wouldn't be easy. many people told us it would be impossible. we knew it was unlikely, but still worth doing. a remarkable group of researchers and engineers joined the effort from inside and outside meta. every single person came in, picked up a shovel, and got to work with earnestness and urgency. nobody asked whose job it was.

we assembled a team of the most brilliant people i have ever had the opportunity to work with (and remember, i was an HRT intern 🙃). i am surrounded by ambitious, visionary, technically excellent, hard-working, pragmatic, thoughtful scientists, engineers, and product folks—people who will chase a weird loss spike past midnight just because they need to know why. these models are the product of their passion, hard work, and brilliance.

somewhat paradoxically, when we started TBD, we set a principle of no deadlines. we knew we had an astronomical amount of work ahead of us—across pretraining, post-training, RL, multimodal, infrastructure, safety, data, AND frontier research. there was no use setting arbitrary timelines—we just had to get to work, be thoughtful, and build the foundations of a frontier research effort in record time. and run after run, this team did exactly that.

our researchers are magicians. i can only describe building these models with this team as a wondrous journey of scientific discovery. i am constantly amazed by what we can accomplish with scaling. i will remember this past year for the rest of my life—the late nights, the broken runs, the evals that came back better than any of us dared to hope. watching this team create wonder after wonder has been a true and deep gift.

more than just the models we released this week, we have built a machine that builds new models. it often sounds like a cop-out to say labs can just turn the crank to keep scaling, but now i have seen it first-hand. sure, it's a lot of work and a careful process, but we have built a scalable system to keep advancing at the frontier, and i am really proud of how fast this team keeps making these models better.

lastly, i get to work with researchers who care deeply about how their work benefits humanity. it's easy to forget when everything is changing so fast, but the whole damn point is to make people's lives better. time and time again, i have seen our researchers, engineers, and product folks build our technology with care so it can truly be good for the world—whether that's building the best models for muse, thoughtfully open-sourcing strong models, or making sure the alignment and security of our systems are rock solid. this is a team of people who never forget there's a real person on the other side of every prompt.

thank you to everyone at MSL for being part of this crazy journey over the past year. i'm so grateful for every one of you, and our work is not done!

fullText:
I want to propose a simple architecture that can eliminate a lot of mess and confusion. 

This can help make bot/code/work modes work cohesively and transparently. It can allow to move between local and cloud very easily.

The idea is very simple: 

Just enable shared file system between cloud and local.

This can be done by dropbox like file sync service that gets automatically mounted in cloud VM and by desktop app.

This can be combined with version control provider that is both available in cloud VM and locally.

You can use shared system to store encrypted secrets that agents are allowed access to. You can use it to store artifacts, memory and anything else agent will needs.

The version control system is for developer crowd so they can turn off their laptop and things can transparently move to cloud VM. This is already done by Claude (they have done great job unifying Work/Code/Bot modes).

However, shared file system is missing which can enable more cool features for OpenAI as well as Muse.
